messages.subject: Killing Rserve instance - a running (forever...) eval needing to be canceled
messages.subject_clean: Killing Rserve instance - a running (forever...) eval needing to be canceled
messages.body_plain:
Hi all!

I am struggling with how to abort an "eval" that is about to take forever. Closing the connection, of course closes the socket be the Rserve instance related to it continue processing. 

I tried to find PID of the related process, but for now, I only managed to obtain the main instance PID using the server startup option "--RS-pidfile rserve_pid.txt", which doesn't help, since, if I "kill -9 pid", will kill an instance, but not the one that is actually processing (the one created while opening the connection).

Is there a way to abort an eval or kill an entire targeted instance of Rserve (even ungracefully)?
Otherwise, what does anyone of you know what would be a "not to ugly" approach to hack the library (Rserve or Rsession) to achieve this?

Example of eval that will never end: "library(ptw); asysm(some_double_vector_object, 10.0, 0.0)".

Thanks a lot by advance for your help and time.

Best Regards
Gauthier

messages.subject: Authentication with Rserve 1.8-1?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm having problems with the configuriation options in Rserv.conf of Rserve version 1.8-1. Connecting is no problem,  I simply can't get the server to refusing the connection without a user/password.
I searched the web and the mailing list, and tried different very basic settings in Rserv.conf.

For example this one (see below):
http://dev.mygrid.org.uk/wiki/display/tav250/Rserve+installation+and+deployment

Environment and versions:
- Virtual machine with CentOS 6.4 64bit, R 3.1.0 64 bit and Rserve 1.8-1
- REngine Java client on Windows

File: /etc/Rserv.conf:

pwdfile <password_file>
remote enable
auth required
encoding utf8

File /etc/Rserv.pwd:

alanw frog
stian fishsoup

Behaviour:
Startup of Rserve: from within the R console with Rserve(debug=TRUE) -> OK
Connecting to Rserve from Java client (remote connection), running functions -> OK
Changing port address in Rserv.conf -> OK (so the conf file is read)

But from the Java client I can always connect to Rserve without a user/password.
In the RConnection the authReq flag always stays false. When stepping through the method initWithSocket(Socket sock, RSession session) everything works fine, but there seems to be no authentication in the protocol.

This is quite  frustrating.

BTW: Is there a complete list of options for the latest version available?  And more examples for using the java client?

Thanks,
Friedrich Schuster

messages.body_plain:
Up!
Since I don't get any response, I suppose my question wasn't clear enough, or seemed pointless. So I'll explain it a bit differently:
 I need to perform R evals in a multi-threaded way, which is something Rserve provides quite well.But, if the eval of one instance takes too long, I need to be able to shutdown the instance which is computing the blocking eval. As far as I tested, the given instance will refuse to shutdown until the eval is done (apparently, it needs to fetch the result, before listening again). So here is my question:Is there a way get a java handle on the blocking instance (something like a Process object), such that I can brute force kill/terminate the eval (something like process.destroy())?In other words, when I ask for an eval (create a connection, throw a command), how do I establish a relationship between the eval being processed, and the instance of Rsere related to it, via java?Or did I miss something about Rserve which already allows to deal with this kind of needs?Note: I already tried to run everything (all evals) via serverEval() instead of the regular eval, which runs the computations on the main instance, but this is, of course, not satisfying as it uses only one process (the main one). That one I can kill, but my main goal was to be able to shutdown individually a blocking eval, running on an individual instance. And, naturally, keep advantage of my 8 CPU cores, that is to say, preserve the parallelism. There is no point to use Rserve otherwise (JRI engine would be more than sufficient in this case).Note: I would like to avoid this kind of things (thread), dealing with several instances of the main server itself, on different ports. That is not an option.I hope I made myself clear enough to get an answer or helpful comment. If not, please ask for details. 

Thanks so much by advance.

      De : g b <golgauthic at yahoo.fr>
 À : "stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de" <stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de>

I am struggling with how to abort an "eval" that is about to take forever. Closing the connection, of course closes the socket be the Rserve instance related to it continue processing. 
I tried to find PID of the related process, but for now, I only managed to obtain the main instance PID using the server startup option "--RS-pidfile rserve_pid.txt", which doesn't help, since, if I "kill -9 pid", will kill an instance, but not the one that is actually processing (the one created while opening the connection).
Is there a way to abort an eval or kill an entire targeted instance of Rserve (even ungracefully)?Otherwise, what does anyone of you know what would be a "not to ugly" approach to hack the library (Rserve or Rsession) to achieve this?
Example of eval that will never end: "library(ptw); asysm(some_double_vector_object, 10.0, 0.0)".
Thanks a lot by advance for your help and time.
Best RegardsGauthier

messages.subject: Re: Killing Rserve instance - a running (forever...) eval needing to be canceled
messages.subject_clean: Killing Rserve instance - a running (forever...) eval needing to be canceled
messages.body_plain:
If I understand you correctly you want to kill a particular Rserve client session, not a server. That is typically done by opening another session and sending a TERM signal:

REngine e = (REngine) new RConenction();
int pid = e.eval("Sys.getpid()").asInteger();
e.eval("...random code ...")

// from another thread:

REngine e2 =(REngine) new RConnection();
e.eval("tools::pskill("+pid+")");
e.close();

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Encryption with Rserve 1.8-1?
messages.body_plain:
> On Nov 25, 2014, at 4:32 AM, Friedrich Schuster <Friedrich.Schuster at analytical-software.de> wrote:
> 
> Hi,
> 
> Looks like I can't find info on encryption with Rserve (Dev version 1.8-1). 
> 
> Has encryption to be compiled at compile/installation time at the Rserve server? 

It is compiled by default if OpenSSL is available.


> Is it possible to use an encrypted connection with the REngine java client? 
> 

There are three ways to use the encryption:

a) QAP over TLS - this is the same protocol as used by default Rserve (QAP), but it is conducted over a TLS-secured channel.

b) wss (WebSockets over SSL) or https upgrade - standard HTTPS/WSS protocols wrapping QAP (typically use by JS interfaces to Rserve)

c) RSA-encyrpted authentication. This only affect the authentication pieces with uses RSA encryption, the actual payload after authentication is no longer encrypted (for speed).

The Java client doesn't support any of the above directly, but the RConnection API allows the application so supply the Socket, so you can create a connection using SSLSocket and then instantiate RConnection to use the option a) above.

Cheers,
Simon
